title: Normalized scalar-six coefficient and extension comparison interfaces
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $a:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ a coefficient map [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Use the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and identified-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $T_a^X=L\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$, $P_\Lambda(f)=D(f^*)$, and define the tower comparison $T_a^X T_b^X\cong T_{ba}^X$ as the adjunction conjugate of restriction-of-scalars transitivity. Define the canonical pullback comparison morphism $P_\Lambda(f)T_a^X\to T_a^YP_{\Lambda'}(f)$ as the scalar-adjunction mate of the restriction/inverse-image comparison. Define $\operatorname{ScalarSixGeometry}$ as the coefficient-ring and internal/sectionwise module presentation identifications: the coefficient adjunct is the published coefficient pushforward on every section, the direct-image comparison is identity on sections, and the inverse-image comparison is its adjunction mate. Define $\operatorname{ScalarSixPullbackData}$ to consist of an isomorphism $\theta$ whose forward map is that canonical pullback morphism, satisfying the inverse-image-composition and scalar-tower equations. In the standing separated finite-type scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], transport the exact locally closed extension of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] through the fixed internal/sectionwise module equivalence; define its restriction isomorphism and immersion compositor by cancelling the equivalence unit/counit and using the published restriction and gamma. Define the ordinary open comparison interface by its inverse-image adjunction-mate normalization, its termwise derived comparison, and the termwise transported closed direct image and closed comparison. Finally define $\operatorname{ScalarSixExtensionData}$ as existence of scalar/locally-closed-extension isomorphisms whose restriction is inverse $\theta$, compatible with the published immersion compositor, normalized open comparison, closed comparison, and scalar tower. These are definitions of normalized comparison data and canonical maps; no existence assertion for geometry, $\theta$, or extension comparison data is included.
